what_it_does: A vitamin A derivative that helps smooth texture, fine lines, and uneven tone.
summary_short: Retinol is an over-the-counter retinoid used for visible signs of photoaging, including fine lines, rough texture, and uneven pigmentation. It is less potent than prescription retinoids, but often better tolerated when formulated well and introduced gradually.
summary_long:
Retinol is a cosmetic form of vitamin A used to improve the look of photoaged skin. In skin, retinoids influence cell turnover and help regulate processes involved in texture, pigmentation, and collagen support, which is why retinol is commonly used for fine lines, roughness, and uneven tone.

The most relevant clinical evidence in the provided sources is a 2022 review focused on cosmetic retinol, which reports improvement in fine lines and wrinkles, hyperpigmentation, roughness, and overall photoaged appearance with properly formulated retinol products [PMID:unknown]. The review also notes that prescription retinoids are generally more potent, but retinol can be a more accessible and tolerable option for many consumers.

Retinol can cause dryness, peeling, stinging, and temporary redness, especially when first started or used too often. Many users do best by applying it at night, starting a few times per week, and pairing it with a bland moisturizer. Daily sunscreen is especially important, since retinol is usually used to address sun-related aging and irritation can make skin feel more sensitive.

Retinol is commonly paired with moisturizers, barrier-supporting ingredients, and sunscreen. It may be harder to tolerate when layered with strong exfoliating acids, abrasive scrubs, or other irritating actives in the same routine, so many people alternate those products rather than using everything at once.

The provided evidence is strongest for cosmetic use in photoaging, not for every vitamin A-related claim. Several listed abstracts focus on dietary retinol or retinol-binding proteins rather than topical skincare, so they are less useful for judging how a face product will perform.
quick_facts: Used for fine lines and texture
Best used at night (breaks down with UV exposure)
Pair with moisturizer and sunscreen (if used during the day)
